title: Normalized comparison of strict quotient towers before localization
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a scheme $T$. Use the completed coefficient sheaf $R$ and its finite quotient sheaves $S_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and the Cont-presentation completion $B$ with finite coefficient sheaves $L_n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], where index $n$ denotes exponent $n+1$. Let $q_n$ be quotient ring isomorphisms normalized on quotient representatives as in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison]; let $e:B\simeq R$ obey $e\pi_n=\pi_n^B e_n$, where $e_n:L_n\simeq S_n$ is the published level comparison determined by $q_n$. For every cochain complex $P$ of $R$-module sheaves, with no K-flatness or boundedness hypothesis, the strict complex of towers formed by restricting $P$ along $e$, applying the ordinary Cont quotient-tower functor and restricting back along $e^{-1}$ is isomorphic to the unrestricted ordinary quotient tower of $P$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. There is such an isomorphism $r$ whose degree-$i$, level-$n$ map sends the sheafified local pure tensor $b\otimes x$ to $e_n(b)\otimes x$, for every site object and local sections $b,x$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This is a statement in complexes of strict diagrams before sections and before derived localization.

proof.text: Define the degreewise and levelwise forward map by b tensor x maps to e_n(b) tensor x. The displayed completed-projection equation identifies the two balancing relations, so the presheaf maps descend and sheafify. Define the reverse map using e_n inverse. Both composites fix every pure tensor, so tensor generation and sheafification uniqueness make them identity maps.

Naturality in the original module makes the maps commute with every differential. The normalized presentation comparison gives quotient-transition compatibility for the e_n. On each pure tensor this is exactly compatibility of the forward and inverse maps with the adjacent strict quotient transitions. Every arrow in the inverse sequence is a composite of these, so the maps assemble to inverse maps of complexes of strict towers. Their construction gives the required section formula, also for zero and unbounded complexes.

theorem strictPresentationComparison (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (T : Scheme.{u})
    (q : ∀ n : ℕ, PbcIntegralRing l E ⧸ (pbcIntegralDatum l E).ideal ^ (n + 1) ≃+*
      ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
    (hq : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : PbcIntegralRing l E), q n (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x) =
      ULift.up (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x.down))
    (e : pbcAdicCompletion T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ≅
      completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E T)
    (he : ∀ n : ℕ, e.hom ≫ completedIntegralCommRingProjectionUnrestricted l E T n =
      pbcAdicProjection T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n ≫
        (IntegralCoefficientPresentation.level l E T q n).hom)
    (P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E T) ℤ) :
    ∃ r :
      (((pbcRestrict e.hom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        completedReductionComplexTowerFunctor T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ⋙
          ((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ _ _).obj (pbcRestrict e.inv)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≅
      (((Functor.ofOpSequence
        (X := fun n ↦ unrestrictedIntegralComplexFunctor l E T n)
        (unrestrictedIntegralTransition l E T)).flip ⋙
          (HomologicalComplex.functorEquivalence
            (integralTowerModules l E T) (.up ℤ) ℕᵒᵖ).inverse).obj P),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ) (U : T.ProEtᵒᵖ)
        (b : ((pbcAdicRings T (pbcIntegralDatum l E)).obj (op n)).obj.obj U)
        (x : (P.X i).val.obj U),
        (((r.hom.f i).app (op n)).val.app U)
            (reductionTensorSection T
              (completedReductionProjection T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n)
              ((pbcRestrict e.hom).obj (P.X i)) U b x) =
          unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E T n (P.X i) U
            ((IntegralCoefficientPresentation.level l E T q n).hom.hom.app U b) x
